Gold climbs above $4,100 as falling yields, softer labor costs support bullion - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were higher in early U.S. trading Thursday, extending Wednesday's sharp gains as lower Treasury yields and a softer U.S. dollar continued to support precious metals following Democrats' sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections. Fresh economic data showing stronger productivity growth and declining unit labor costs provided additional relief from inflation concerns, although resilient employment conditions and expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December continued to limit the bullish implications for bullion. At the latest verified morning price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,119.50 an ounce, up $60.30, or 1.49%, while spot silver was trading near $52.390, up $0.294, or 0.56%. Gold had earlier reached $4,146.63, its highest level since Oct. 20, extending its recovery from October's steep correction. Thursday's U.S. economic reports provided fresh evidence of improving labor productivity and moderating cost pressure, alongside continued resilience in the employment market. Nonfarm business productivity increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 3.6% in the third quarter, accelerating from an upwardly revised 2.1% in the second quarter. Output increased 3.7%, while hours worked advanced just 0.1%. Unit labor costs declined at a 0.7% annualized rate, reversing the previous quarter's revised 1.9% increase, as productivity growth outpaced the 2.9% increase in hourly compensation. The decline in unit labor costs suggests that improving efficiency is helping businesses absorb wage increases without placing equivalent upward pressure on prices, although the relationship between productivity and consumer inflation is not immediate.

items.titleEn: gold prices holding above $4,100 as weekly jobless claims rise by 189k
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices are holding initial support above $4,100 an ounce, but downside risks appear to be growing as positive momentum in the U.S. labor market picks up, with the number of American workers applying for first-time unemployment benefits dropping sharply last week. Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ending October 31, the Labor Department announced Thursday. The data was better than expected, as consensus estimates had called for a rise to 197,000. The gold market is not seeing any significant reaction to the solid labor market data, but prices remain off their session highs. Spot gold last traded at $4,120.60 an ounce, up 1.5% on the day.

Gold market holding solid gains even as BoE raises interest rates due to rising inflation
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Persistent inflation pressures continue to take their toll on the gold market as central banks are forced to adopt hawkish monetary policies, with the Bank of England being the latest example. On Thursday, in a widely anticipated move, the Bank of England raised its Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4%. The central bank also projects inflation will move higher next year. “The conflict in the Middle East is now in its ninth month. Global energy prices have continued to rise from an already elevated level. UK CPI inflation increased to 3.5% in September. It is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year. It is then projected to fall as the impact of rising energy prices on 12-month inflation rates fades, and still restrictive monetary policy bears down on inflation,” the central bank said.
